1	export type Cell = [x: number, y: number];
2	
3	const isWithinOneStep = (coordinate: number, otherCoordinate: number): boolean =>
4	  Math.abs(otherCoordinate - coordinate) <= 1;
5	
6	const isNeighborOf = ([x, y]: Cell, [otherX, otherY]: Cell): boolean =>
7	  isWithinOneStep(x, otherX) &&
8	  isWithinOneStep(y, otherY) &&
9	  !(otherX === x && otherY === y);
10	
11	const countLivingNeighbors = (cell: Cell, livingCells: Cell[]): number =>
12	  livingCells.filter((other) => isNeighborOf(cell, other)).length;
13	
14	const survives = (livingNeighbors: number): boolean =>
15	  livingNeighbors >= 2 && livingNeighbors <= 3;
16	
17	const neighborsOf = ([x, y]: Cell): Cell[] => [
18	  [x - 1, y - 1],
19	  [x, y - 1],
20	  [x + 1, y - 1],
21	  [x - 1, y],
22	  [x + 1, y],
23	  [x - 1, y + 1],
24	  [x, y + 1],
25	  [x + 1, y + 1],
26	];
27	
28	const isLiving = (cell: Cell, livingCells: Cell[]): boolean =>
29	  livingCells.some(([x, y]) => x === cell[0] && y === cell[1]);
30	
31	const bornCells = (livingCells: Cell[]): Cell[] =>
32	  livingCells
33	    .flatMap(neighborsOf)
34	    .filter(
35	      (candidate) =>
36	        !isLiving(candidate, livingCells) &&
37	        countLivingNeighbors(candidate, livingCells) === 3,
38	    );
39	
40	export const nextGeneration = (livingCells: Cell[]): Cell[] => [
41	  ...livingCells.filter((cell) =>
42	    survives(countLivingNeighbors(cell, livingCells)),
43	  ),
44	  ...bornCells(livingCells),
45	];

All 7 tests green — Rule 1 satisfied. Now the refactoring analysis.

**Step 1 — Naming Evaluation (first priority)**

| Name | Reveals intent? | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| `nextGeneration` | Yes — matches domain language | Keep |
| `isWithinOneStep` | Yes | Keep |
| `isNeighborOf` | Yes | Keep |
| `countLivingNeighbors` | Yes | Keep |
| `survives` | Yes — reads as `survives(livingNeighbors)` | Keep |
| `neighborsOf` | Yes | Keep |
| `isLiving` | Yes | Keep |
| `bornCells` | Yes — cells born this generation | Keep |

Naming is already good after the previous cycles. No rename warranted.

**Step 2 — Rule 3 violation found: conceptual duplication of "same cell"**

The identity comparison between two cells is expressed twice, in two different notations:

- `game-of-life.ts:9` — `!(otherX === x && otherY === y)`
- `game-of-life.ts:29` — `x === cell[0] && y === cell[1]`

Same knowledge, two representations. The second also leaks tuple indexing (`cell[0]`, `cell[1]`), which hurts Rule 2.

content.text:
All 7 tests pass and `tsc --noEmit` is clean.

**APP Mass Calculation**

Scope: the two functions touched (`isNeighborOf`, `isLiving`) plus the extracted `isSameCell`.

Before — mass 52:
- `isNeighborOf`: bindings 12 (×1) + invocations 7 (×2 = 14) = **26**
- `isLiving`: bindings 9 (×1) + constants 2 (index literals `0`, `1`, ×1) + invocations 5 (×2 = 10) + loop 1 (`.some`, ×5) = **26**

After — mass 53:
- `isSameCell`: bindings 8 + invocations 3 (×2 = 6) = **14**
- `isNeighborOf`: bindings 14 + invocations 6 (×2 = 12) = **26**
- `isLiving`: bindings 6 + invocations 1 (×2 = 2) + loop 1 (×5) = **13**

Mass change: 52 → 53 (Δ +1, essentially flat). Rule 2 trumps APP here — a one-point mass increase buys the elimination of a duplicated concept and removes raw tuple indexing from the code. `isLiving` on its own dropped 26 → 13.

**Simple Design Rules applied**
1. Tests pass — 7/7 green before and after, verified between each of the two steps.
2. Reveals intent — `isLiving` now reads "some living cell is the same cell", instead of the opaque `x === cell[0] && y === cell[1]`. Names all evaluated first; none needed changing.
3. No duplication — the "two cells are the same cell" concept had two representations; now one, `isSameCell`, used by both `isNeighborOf` and `isLiving`.
4. Fewest elements — one new element added. Justified: it is the shared vocabulary that removes the duplication. `isNeighborOf` gained a block body so it can name both the whole cells and their coordinates; the alternative (a second `isWithinOneStepOnBothAxes` helper) cost an extra element and mass 55, so I chose the cheaper form.

Note carried forward, not acted on: `bornCells` in `/home/experimenter/experiments/runs/2026-07-25_23-41-37_game-of-life-example-mapping_v4-exact-subagents_opus-5-no-thinking/src/game-of-life.ts` still emits duplicate coordinates when a dead cell is reached from several living neighbors. No current test demands uniqueness, so deduplicating now would be implementing ahead. The upcoming "block still life" and blinker tests will likely force it — that is the right moment.

Refactor Phase Complete
- Refactoring: extracted `isSameCell`; reused in `isNeighborOf` and `isLiving`
- Mass change: 52 → 53 (Δ +1; `isLiving` alone 26 → 13)
- Tests: 7 passing, 4 todo. Typecheck clean.
